title: The leak scan passes a url password that holds an angle bracket, because URL_USERINFO's password class excludes < and > and _value reads any < or > as a placeholder
goal: kbcommon.structured_secrets reports a url whose password holds an angle bracket but is not a placeholder whole, as redact.redact now takes it

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kbcommon; r=kbcommon.structured_secrets("https://jan:a<b>cccccc@srv01.corp.contoso.com/x"); print(r); sys.exit(0 if r else 1)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbcommon as k
ph=k.structured_secrets('https://jan:<password>@srv01.corp.contoso.com/x')
bad=k.structured_secrets('https://jan:a<b>cccccc@srv01.corp.contoso.com/x')
print(ph,bad);sys.exit(0 if bad and not ph else 1)

notes: Found while fixing BG-5dcfyrks (redact side, a redact-only URL_USERINFO_ANGLE shape in _tools/redact.py). The fix is in kbcommon.py, which the in-flight BG-fwqcimiv also changes: order it after that item. Outbound paths (referrers file_hits leak_hits, read 2026-11-09): structured_secrets is read by kbcommon.leak_hits and kbpublic's tracked-file scan (kbpublic.py:559), so every caller of leak_hits and file_hits sees the new report: publish, contribute and the sync range gate (shipped scan), bl_check, census, check.py, bl_land, ql_store, ql_research, kbingest, kbtail. All take the report through one function in kbcommon.py, the only file changed; none passes a different scan for this shape. Planted check runs a whole placeholder (still no hit) and an angle-bracket password (a hit).
